title.zh: 卷八十 列傳第十八: 熙宗二子濟安 道濟 斜卯阿里 突合速 烏延蒲盧渾 赤盞暉 大㚖本名撻不野 磐本名蒲速越 阿離補子:方
title.en: Volume 80 Biographies 18: Xi Zong and Two Sons Jian, Dao Ji, Xie Maoali, Tu Hesu, Wuyan Puluhun, Chi Zhanhui, Da Gao Formerly Named Tabuye, Pan Formerly Named Pusuyue, a Libu Son: Fang
title.raw: 卷八十 列傳第十八: 熙宗二子濟安 道濟 斜卯阿里 突合速 烏延蒲盧渾 赤盞暉 大㚖本名撻不野 磐本名蒲速越 阿離補子:方 Volume 80 Biographies 18: Xi Zong and Two Sons Jian, Dao Ji, Xie Maoali, Tu Hesu, Wuyan Puluhun, Chi Zhanhui, Da Gao Formerly Named Tabuye, Pan Formerly Named Pusuyue, a Libu Son: Fang

sentences.zh: 熙宗二子

translations.literal: The two sons of Xi Zong
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zong's Two Sons

sentences.zh: 熙宗諸子：悼平皇后生太子濟安，賢妃生魏王道濟。

translations.literal: The sons of Xi Zong: Empress Daoping bore the Crown Prince Ji'an; the Virtuous Consort bore the Prince of Wei, Dao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zong's sons were as follows: Empress Daoping gave birth to Crown Prince Ji'an; the Virtuous Consort gave birth to the Prince of Wei, Dao Ji.

sentences.zh: 濟安，皇統二年二月戊子生於天開殿。

translations.literal: Ji'an was born on the wuzi day of the second month of the second year of Huangtong in the Tiankai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an was born on the wuzi day of the second month in the second year of Huangtong (1142) in the Tiankai Hall.

sentences.zh: 上年二十四始有皇子，喜甚，遣使馳報明德宮太皇太后。

translations.literal: The Emperor was twenty-four and had a prince for the first time; he was exceedingly glad and sent messengers posthaste to report to the Grand Empress Dowager at the Mingde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was twenty-four and had his first son; overjoyed, he dispatched messengers at once to inform the Grand Empress Dowager at the Mingde Palace.

sentences.zh: 五日命名，大赦天下。

translations.literal: On the fifth day he was named; a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the child was named, and a general amnesty was declared for the entire realm.

sentences.zh: 三月甲寅，告天地宗廟。

translations.literal: On jiayin in the third month, he reported to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the third month, the birth was announced to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，翦鬌，奏告天地宗廟。

translations.literal: On dingsi his hair was cut; memorials were presented to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi his hair was ritually cut, and the rite was reported to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 戊午，冊爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On wuwu he was invested as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he was formally installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 封皇后父太尉胡塔爲王，賜人口、馬牛五百、駝五十、羊五千。

translations.literal: The empress's father, Grand Marshal Huta, was enfeoffed as king and granted households, five hundred horses and cattle, fifty camels, and five thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father, Grand Marshal Huta, was created a prince and given households plus five hundred horses and cattle, fifty camels, and five thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 隨朝職官並遷一資，皆有賜。

translations.literal: All officials at court were advanced one rank in salary grade, and all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Every official at court was promoted one salary grade and received gifts.

sentences.zh: 已未，詔天下。

translations.literal: On jiwei an edict was issued to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei an edict was promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，濟安病劇，上與皇后幸佛寺焚香，流涕哀禱，曲赦五百里內罪囚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Ji'an's illness grew grave; the Emperor and the empress visited a Buddhist temple to burn incense, weeping and praying in grief, and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners within five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Ji'an fell gravely ill. The emperor and empress went to a Buddhist temple to burn incense, weeping as they prayed, and granted a partial amnesty to prisoners within five hundred li.

sentences.zh: 是夜，薨。

translations.literal: That night he died.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died.

sentences.zh: 諡英悼太子，葬興陵之側，上送至烏只黑水而還。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Yingdao Crown Prince and buried beside Xingling; the Emperor escorted the funeral as far as Wuzhi Heishui and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Yingdao Crown Prince and buried beside Xingling; the emperor accompanied the funeral procession to Wuzhi Heishui before returning.

sentences.zh: 命工塑其像于儲慶寺，上與皇后幸寺安置之。

translations.literal: Artisans were ordered to cast his image at Chuqing Temple; the Emperor and the empress visited the temple to install it.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans were ordered to sculpt his image at Chuqing Temple, and the emperor and empress went there to install it.

sentences.zh: 海陵毀上京宮室，寺亦隨毀。

translations.literal: Hailing destroyed the palaces at Shangjing, and the temple was destroyed along with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing razed the palaces at Shangjing, the temple was destroyed as well.

sentences.zh: 道濟，皇統三年，命爲中京留守，以直學士阿懶爲都提點，張玄素爲同提點，左右輔導之。

translations.literal: Dao Ji, in the third year of Huangtong, was appointed Zhongjing garrison commander; the Direct Academician Alan was made chief superintendent, Zhang Xuansu associate superintendent, to guide him on either hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangtong, Dao Ji was appointed garrison commander of Zhongjing; the Direct Academician Alan served as chief superintendent and Zhang Xuansu as associate superintendent to tutor him on either side.

sentences.zh: 俄封魏王，封其母爲賢妃。

translations.literal: Shortly he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, and his mother was made Virtuous Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was created Prince of Wei, and his mother was raised to Virtuous Consort.

sentences.zh: 初居外，至是養之宮中。

translations.literal: At first he had lived outside the palace; now he was reared within it.
translations.idiomatic: He had first lived outside the palace; now he was brought up within it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，熙宗怒殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Xi Zong, in anger, had him put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xi Zong, in a fit of rage, had him executed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：國初制度未立，太宗、熙宗皆自諳班勃極烈即帝位。

translations.literal: The encomium says: At the founding of the state institutions were not yet fixed; both Taizong and Xi Zong ascended the throne from the post of Anban Bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: In the early days of the dynasty the institutions were still unsettled; both Taizong and Xi Zong had taken the throne straight from the Anban Bojilie seat.

sentences.zh: 諳班勃極烈者，漢語雲最尊官也。

translations.literal: Anban Bojilie—in Chinese it means the most exalted office.
translations.idiomatic: Anban Bojilie, in Chinese, means the most exalted office.

sentences.zh: 熙宗立濟安爲皇太子，始正名位，定制度焉。

translations.literal: Xi Zong installed Ji'an as crown prince, thereby for the first time rectifying titles and ranks and fixing the institutions.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Zong installed Ji'an as crown prince, he for the first time regularized titles and ranks and established the succession system.

sentences.zh: 斜卯阿里

translations.literal: Xiemao Ali
translations.idiomatic: Xiemao Ali

sentences.zh: 斜卯阿里，父渾坦，穆宗時內附，數有戰功。

translations.literal: Xiemao Ali—his father was Huntan, who submitted to the Jin in Muzong's time and won many battles.
translations.idiomatic: Xiemao Ali's father Huntan had submitted during Muzong's reign and won many battles.

sentences.zh: 阿里年十七，從其伯父胡麻谷討詐都，獲其弟沙里只。

translations.literal: Ali at seventeen followed his uncle Humagu to campaign against Zhadu and captured his younger brother Shalizhi.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen Ali followed his uncle Humagu against Zhadu and captured Zhadu's younger brother Shalizhi.

sentences.zh: 高麗築九城於曷懶甸，渾坦攻之，遇敵於木里門甸，力戰久之，阿里挺槍馳刺其將於陣中，敵遂潰。

translations.literal: Goryeo built nine fortresses in the Yalian district; Huntan attacked them and met the enemy at Mulimen district; after fighting long and hard, Ali spurred forward with his spear and ran down their general in the midst of the array, and the enemy broke.
translations.idiomatic: When Goryeo built nine fortresses in the Yalian district, Huntan attacked them. At Mulimen the fighting dragged on until Ali charged into the enemy line and speared their general; the foe then collapsed.

sentences.zh: 渾坦與石適歡合兵于徒門水，阿里首敗敵兵，取其二城。

translations.literal: Huntan joined forces with Shi Shihuan at Tumen River; Ali was first to defeat the enemy army and took two of their cities.
translations.idiomatic: Huntan united with Shi Shihuan at the Tumen River; Ali led the assault, routed the enemy, and captured two cities.

sentences.zh: 高麗入寇，以我兵屯守要害，不得進，乃還。

translations.literal: Goryeo invaded, but because our troops held the strategic points they could not advance and therefore withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo invaded, but Jin troops held the key passes and blocked their advance, so they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 阿里追及于曷懶水，高麗人爭走冰上，阿里乘之，殺略幾盡，遂合兵于石適歡。

translations.literal: Ali overtook them at Yalian River; the Goryeo men scrambled onto the ice, and Ali pressed the attack and slaughtered nearly all of them, then rejoined Shi Shihuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ali caught them at the Yalian River. The Goryeo soldiers fled onto the ice; he pressed the pursuit and killed nearly all of them, then rejoined Shi Shihuan.

sentences.zh: 道遇敵兵五萬，擊走之。

translations.literal: On the road they met fifty thousand enemy troops and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: On the march they met fifty thousand enemy troops and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 又與石適歡遇敵七萬，阿里先登，奮擊大敗之。

translations.literal: Again, together with Shi Shihuan, they met seventy thousand enemy troops; Ali led the charge and fought fiercely, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Again, with Shi Shihuan, they met seventy thousand enemy troops; Ali led the assault and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 石適歡曰：「汝一日之間，三破重敵，功豈可忘。」

translations.literal: Shi Shihuan said: "In a single day you have thrice broken heavy enemy forces—how could such merit be forgotten?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shihuan said, "In one day you have thrice broken major enemy forces—such merit cannot be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 乃厚賜之。

translations.literal: and thereupon rewarded him generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 斡塞、烏睹本攻駝吉城，阿里鑿墉爲門，日已暮，不可入，以兵守之，旦日遂取其城。

translations.literal: Wosai and Wuduben attacked Tuoji city; Ali cut through the wall to make a gate; night had fallen and entry was impossible, so he left troops to hold it, and at dawn took the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wosai and Wuduben attacked Tuoji, Ali breached the wall to open a gate. Night had fallen, so he could not enter at once; he left troops to hold the breach and took the city at dawn.

sentences.zh: 烏睹本以被甲並乘馬賜之。

translations.literal: Wuduben bestowed on him armor and a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wuduben rewarded him with armor and a horse.

sentences.zh: 從攻下甯江州，授猛安。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack that captured Ningjiang Prefecture and was appointed meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Ningjiang Prefecture and was appointed meng'an.

sentences.zh: 又從攻信州、賓州，皆克之。

translations.literal: He again followed in attacks on Xinzhou and Binzhou; both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined attacks on Xinzhou and Binzhou, and both fell.

sentences.zh: 遼人來攻孛堇忽沙里城，阿里率百餘騎救之。

translations.literal: Liao troops came to attack Bojin Hushali city; Ali led a little more than a hundred horsemen to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao forces attacked Bojin Hushali, Ali led a little over a hundred horsemen to its relief.

sentences.zh: 遼兵數萬，阿里兵少，乃令軍士裂衣多爲旗幟，出山谷間，遼兵望見，遁去。

translations.literal: The Liao army numbered in the tens of thousands while Ali's force was few; he therefore ordered the soldiers to tear cloth and make many banners, and marched out through the mountain valleys; the Liao troops saw them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao army numbered in the tens of thousands while Ali had only a small force. He had his men tear cloth into many banners and march out through the valleys; when the Liao troops saw them, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 蘇、復州叛，眾至十萬。

translations.literal: Su and Fu prefectures rebelled; their forces reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Su and Fu prefectures rebelled, and their forces swelled to one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 旁近女直皆保于太尉胡沙家，築壘爲固。

translations.literal: Nearby Jurchen all took refuge with Grand Marshal Husha and built fortifications to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby Jurchen bands all took refuge with Grand Marshal Husha and built fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 敵圍之數重，守者糧芻俱盡，牛馬相食其鬃尾，人易子而食。

translations.literal: The enemy besieged them in layer upon layer; the defenders' grain and fodder were exhausted, cattle and horses ate one another's manes and tails, and men exchanged children to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy laid siege in rings upon rings. Grain and fodder ran out; cattle and horses ate one another's manes and tails, and the people exchanged children to eat.

sentences.zh: 夜，縋二人出，告急于阿里。

translations.literal: By night two men were lowered out on ropes to report the emergency to Ali.
translations.idiomatic: That night two men were lowered over the wall on ropes to beg Ali for relief.

sentences.zh: 阿里赴之，內外合擊之，破其眾於辟離密罕水上，剿殺幾盡，水爲之不流。

translations.literal: Ali hastened there; inside and outside they struck together and broke the enemy host on the Pilimihan River, slaughtering nearly all; the water ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: Ali hurried to the spot. Attackers inside and out struck together and shattered the rebel host on the Pilimihan River, slaughtering nearly all of them until the water would not flow.

sentences.zh: 蒲離古胡什吉水、馬韓島凡十余戰，破數十萬眾。

translations.literal: At Puligu, Hushiji River, and Mahan Island he fought more than ten battles in all and broke forces numbering in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Puligu, the Hushiji River, and Mahan Island he fought more than ten battles and broke armies numbering in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 契丹、奚人聚舟千艘，將入於海。

translations.literal: Khitan and Xi gathered a thousand boats, intending to put out to sea.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Xi forces gathered a thousand boats, intending to escape by sea.

sentences.zh: 阿里以二十七舟邀之，中流矢，臥舟中，中夜始蘇。

translations.literal: Ali with twenty-seven boats intercepted them, was struck by an arrow midstream, lay in the boat, and only at midnight came to.
translations.idiomatic: Ali intercepted them with twenty-seven boats, was struck by an arrow midstream, and lay unconscious in his boat until midnight.

sentences.zh: 敵船已入王家島，即夜取海路追及之，敵走險以拒，阿里以騎兵邀擊，再中流矢，力戰不退，竟破之，盡獲其舟。

translations.literal: The enemy boats had already entered Wangjia Island; that same night he took the sea route in pursuit and overtook them; the enemy fled into difficult ground to resist; Ali with cavalry intercepted them, was again struck by an arrow, fought on without yielding, and in the end broke them and captured all their boats.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy boats had already reached Wangjia Island. That same night Ali took the sea route in pursuit, caught them as they fled into difficult ground, and struck with cavalry. He was wounded again but fought on without retreat until he broke them and seized every boat.

sentences.zh: 於是，蘇、復州、婆速路皆平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su and Fu prefectures and the Basu circuit were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Su and Fu prefectures and the Basu circuit were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 攻顯州，下靈山縣，取梁魚務，敗餘睹兵，功皆最。

translations.literal: He attacked Xianzhou, took Lingshan county, seized Liangyuwu, and defeated Yudu's troops; in every exploit his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Xianzhou, took Lingshan County, seized Liangyuwu, and defeated Yudu's army; in every exploit his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 後與散睹魯屯高州，契丹昭古牙、九斤合興中兵數萬攻胡里特寨，阿里以八謀克兵救之。

translations.literal: Later he garrisoned Gaozhou with Sandulu; the Khitan Zhao Guya and Jiujin united Xingzhong troops numbering in the tens of thousands to attack Hulite's stockade; Ali with eight mouke units went to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Later he garrisoned Gaozhou with Sandulu. The Khitan Zhao Guya and Jiujin united tens of thousands of Xingzhong troops to attack Hulite's stockade, and Ali marched to relieve it with eight mouke units.

sentences.zh: 胡里特先往，敗於城下。

translations.literal: Hulite had gone ahead first and was defeated below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Hulite had gone ahead first and was beaten below the walls.

sentences.zh: 阿里指陣前緋衣者二十餘人曰：「此必賊酋也。」

translations.literal: Ali pointed to more than twenty men in scarlet robes before the array and said: "These must surely be the rebel chiefs."
translations.idiomatic: Ali pointed to more than twenty men in scarlet robes before the enemy line and said, "Those must be the rebel chiefs."

sentences.zh: 麾兵奮擊，皆殺之，餘眾大潰。

translations.literal: He waved the troops forward in fierce attack; all were killed, and the rest of the host broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a fierce charge; all were killed, and the rest of the host fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 來州、隰州兵圍胡里特城，聞阿里來救，即解圍去。

translations.literal: Laizhou and Xizhou troops had besieged Hulite's city; when they heard Ali was coming to the rescue they at once lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Laizhou and Xizhou troops had besieged Hulite's city; when they heard Ali was coming to the rescue, they lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 闍母討張覺，有兵出樓峰口山谷間，阿里、散篤魯、忽盧補三猛安擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhamu campaigned against Zhang Jue; enemy troops came out through the valleys at Loufeng Pass; Ali, Sandulu, and Hulubu—the three meng'an—defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhamu campaigned against Zhang Jue, enemy troops emerged through the valleys at Loufeng Pass; Ali, Sandulu, and Hulubu—the three meng'an—routed them.

sentences.zh: 宗望代闍母討張覺，阿里再敗平州兵。

translations.literal: Zongwang replaced Zhamu in campaigning against Zhang Jue; Ali again defeated the Pingzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang replaced Zhamu against Zhang Jue, and Ali again defeated the Pingzhou army.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，阿里別擊宋兵，敗之。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Song, Ali on a separate mission struck Song troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Song, Ali on a separate mission struck Song forces and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 孟陽之役，阿里扼橋渡力戰。

translations.literal: At the battle of Mengyang, Ali held the bridge crossing and fought fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: At Mengyang he held the bridge crossing and fought fiercely.

sentences.zh: 明年，再伐宋，至保州、中山，累破之。

translations.literal: The next year, campaigning against Song again, he reached Baozhou and Zhongshan and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on a second campaign against Song, he reached Baozhou and Zhongshan and repeatedly defeated Song forces.

sentences.zh: 進圍真定，阿里與婁室、豁魯乘風縱火，焚其樓櫓，諸軍畢登，克其城。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Zhending, Ali with Loushi and Huolu rode the wind to set fires, burning the tower shelters; all the armies climbed up together and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to besiege Zhending, Ali with Loushi and Huolu set fires in the wind and burned the tower shelters; all the armies scaled the walls together and took the city.

sentences.zh: 師至河上，粘割胡撒擊走宋人，扼河津，兵數千遂渡河。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Yellow River, Niange Husai drove off the Song men, held the river crossing, and several thousand troops crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached the Yellow River, Niange Husai drove off the Song troops, held the crossing, and several thousand men crossed.

sentences.zh: 諸將分出大名境，阿里破敵四百盡殪，遂圍汴。

translations.literal: The generals divided and issued from the Daming region; Ali destroyed four hundred enemy troops to the last man and then besieged Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The generals fanned out from the Daming region; Ali annihilated four hundred enemy troops and then besieged Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 汴中夜出兵來焚攻具，阿里與謀克常孫陽阿禦之，其眾大潰。

translations.literal: Bian sent troops out by night to burn the siege engines; Ali with the mouke Changsun Yang'a repelled them, and their host broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Bianjing sent troops out by night to burn the siege engines; Ali with the mouke Changsun Yang'a repelled them, and the Song force fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 還攻趙州，降之。

translations.literal: He returned to attack Zhaozhou and received its surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Zhaozhou and received its surrender.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，伐宋主，取陽穀、莘縣，敗海州兵八萬人，海州降。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui, campaigning against the Song ruler, he took Yanggu and Shen county, defeated eighty thousand Haizhou troops, and Haizhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhui, campaigning against the Song emperor, he took Yanggu and Shen County, defeated eighty thousand Haizhou troops, and Haizhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 破賊船萬余於梁山泊。

translations.literal: He destroyed more than ten thousand rebel boats at Liangshan Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed more than ten thousand rebel boats at Liangshan Marsh.

sentences.zh: 招降滕陽、東平、泰山群盜。

translations.literal: He induced the surrender of the bandit gangs of Tengyang, Dongping, and Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He induced the bandit gangs of Tengyang, Dongping, and Mount Tai to surrender.

sentences.zh: 盜攻範縣，擊走之，獲船七百艘。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked Fan county he drove them off and captured seven hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits attacked Fan County, he drove them off and captured seven hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 宗弼攻下睢陽，與烏延蒲盧渾先以二千人往招壽春，具舟淮水上。

translations.literal: Zongbi captured Suiyang; he and Wuyan Puluhun first took two thousand men to summon Shouchun to surrender and prepared boats on the Huai River.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongbi captured Suiyang, he and Wuyan Puluhun took two thousand men ahead to summon Shouchun and prepared boats on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 時康民聚賈船四百與壽春相近，朮列速以騎四百破康民，斬馘數千。

translations.literal: At that time Kang Min had gathered four hundred merchant boats near Shouchun; Zhuliesu with four hundred horsemen broke Kang Min and beheaded or took heads numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Min had gathered four hundred merchant boats near Shouchun; Zhuliesu with four hundred horsemen routed him and killed or captured thousands.

sentences.zh: 與當海、大㚖破賊十萬於淮南。

translations.literal: Together with Danghai and Da Gao he defeated one hundred thousand bandits south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: With Danghai and Da Gao he defeated one hundred thousand rebels south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 比至江，連破宋兵，獲舟二百艘。

translations.literal: By the time they reached the Yangzi they had repeatedly defeated Song troops and captured two hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the Yangzi they had repeatedly defeated Song forces and captured two hundred boats.

sentences.zh: 宗弼至江甯，阿里、蒲盧渾別降廣德軍，先趣杭州。

translations.literal: Zongbi reached Jiangning; Ali and Puluhun on a separate mission received the surrender of Guangde Army and pressed on first toward Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi reached Jiangning, Ali and Puluhun on a separate mission received the surrender of Guangde Army and pressed on toward Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 去杭十餘里，遇宋伏兵二千，取我前驅甲士三十人。

translations.literal: A little more than ten li from Hangzhou they met two thousand Song ambush troops, who captured thirty armored men of our vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: A little over ten li from Hangzhou they met two thousand Song ambushers, who captured thirty armored men of the Jin vanguard.

sentences.zh: 阿里使諸軍去馬搏戰，伏兵敗，皆逼死于水。

translations.literal: Ali ordered all the armies to dismount and fight hand to hand; the ambush troops were defeated and all were driven to their deaths in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Ali ordered his troops to dismount and fight hand to hand; the ambushers were defeated and driven into the water to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 宗弼至余杭，而宋主走明州，阿里與蒲盧渾以精騎四千襲之，破東關兵，濟曹娥江，敗宋兵于高橋鎮。

translations.literal: Zongbi reached Yuhang while the Song ruler fled to Mingzhou; Ali and Puluhun with four thousand picked horsemen raided him, broke the Dongguan troops, crossed the Cao'e River, and defeated Song troops at Gaoqiao town.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi reached Yuhang while the Song emperor fled to Mingzhou; Ali and Puluhun with four thousand picked horsemen raided him, broke the Dongguan garrison, crossed the Cao'e River, and defeated Song forces at Gaoqiao.

sentences.zh: 至明州，頗失利。

translations.literal: At Mingzhou they suffered considerable losses.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzhou they suffered considerable losses.

sentences.zh: 宋主已入於海，乃退軍余姚。

translations.literal: The Song ruler had already put out to sea, so they withdrew the army to Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor had already put to sea, so they withdrew to Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 宗弼使當海濟師，遂下明州，執宋守臣趙伯諤，進至昌國縣。

translations.literal: Zongbi sent Danghai to ferry the army across; they then took Mingzhou, seized the Song defending official Zhao Boyu, and advanced to Changguo county.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi sent Danghai to ferry the army across; they then took Mingzhou, seized the Song defender Zhao Boyu, and advanced to Changguo County.

sentences.zh: 宋主自昌國走溫州，由海路追三百餘里，弗及。

translations.literal: The Song ruler fled from Changguo to Wenzhou; they pursued by sea for more than three hundred li but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor fled from Changguo to Wenzhou; they pursued by sea for more than three hundred li but could not overtake him.

sentences.zh: 遂隳明州，與宗弼俱北歸。

translations.literal: They then dismantled Mingzhou and returned north together with Zongbi.
translations.idiomatic: They then dismantled Mingzhou and returned north with Zongbi.

sentences.zh: 睿宗經略陝西，駐涇州，阿里先取渭州。

translations.literal: Ruizong conducted operations in Shaanxi and halted at Jingzhou; Ali first took Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong conducted operations in Shaanxi and halted at Jingzhou, Ali first took Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 睿宗趨熙河，阿里、斜喝、韓常三猛安爲前軍。

translations.literal: Ruizong pressed toward Xihe; Ali, Xiehe, and Han Chang—the three meng'an—served as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong pressed toward Xihe, Ali, Xiehe, and Han Chang—the three meng'an—led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與高彪監護水運。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he and Gao Biao supervised river transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he and Gao Biao supervised river transport.

sentences.zh: 宋以舟師阻亳州河路，擊敗之，追殺六十餘里，獲其將蕭通。

translations.literal: Song used a fleet to block the Bozhou river route; he defeated them, pursued and killed for more than sixty li, and captured their general Xiao Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Song used a fleet to block the Bozhou river route; he defeated them, pursued for more than sixty li, and captured their general Xiao Tong.

sentences.zh: 破漣水水寨賊，盡得其大船，遂取漣水軍，招徠安輯之。

translations.literal: He broke the bandits of the Lianshui river stockade, took all their large boats, then captured Lianshui Army, and by summoning and soothing brought it to order.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Lianshui river-stockade bandits, seized all their large boats, took Lianshui Army, and pacified the region by summoning people back and reassuring them.

sentences.zh: 天眷間，盜據石州，阿里討之。

translations.literal: During the Tianjuan era bandits held Shizhou; Ali campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjuan era bandits seized Shizhou; Ali campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 粘割胡撒與所部先登，遂克其城，石州平。

translations.literal: Niange Husai and his command were first to scale the walls, and they thereupon took the city; Shizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Niange Husai and his men were first over the wall; they took the city and Shizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再伐宋，阿里已老，督造戰船。

translations.literal: When Zongbi campaigned against Song again, Ali was already old and supervised the construction of war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi campaigned against Song again, Ali was already elderly and supervised the building of war vessels.

sentences.zh: 宋稱臣，詔賜阿里錢千萬。

translations.literal: The Song submitted as vassals; an edict granted Ali ten million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song submitted as vassals, an edict granted Ali ten million in cash.

sentences.zh: 自結髮從軍，大小數十戰，尤習舟楫，江、淮用兵，無役不從，時人以水星目之。

translations.literal: From the time he bound his hair and entered the army he fought in several dozen battles large and small; he was especially skilled in boats and oars; in campaigns on the Yangzi and Huai he took part in every expedition, and people called him the Water Star.
translations.idiomatic: From youth in the army he fought in dozens of battles and was especially skilled with boats; in every Yangzi and Huai campaign he took part, and people nicknamed him the Water Star.

sentences.zh: 爲迭里部節度使，曆順義、泰寧軍，歸德、濟南尹。

translations.literal: He served as military commissioner of the Dieli tribe, passed through Shunyi and Taining Armies, and was governor of Guide and Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military commissioner of the Dieli tribe, held posts in Shunyi and Taining Armies, and was governor of Guide and Jinan.

sentences.zh: 天德初，致仕，加特進，封王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiande he retired, was granted Special Advancement, and was enfeoffed as prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiande he retired, was granted special advancement, and was enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 正隆例封韓國公，召赴闕，命造戰船。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was enfeoffed as Duke of Han, summoned to court, and ordered to build war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was created Duke of Han, recalled to court, and ordered to build war vessels.

sentences.zh: 以疾薨，年七十八，諡智敏。

translations.literal: He died of illness at seventy-eight; his posthumous title was Zhimin.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at seventy-eight and was given the posthumous title Zhimin.

sentences.zh: 阿里性忠直，多智略。

translations.literal: Ali's nature was loyal and upright, and he possessed much resourcefulness in strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ali was loyal and upright, and possessed great strategic resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 兄弟相友愛，家故饒財，以己猛安及財物盡與弟愛拔里。

translations.literal: The brothers were affectionate toward one another; the family was originally wealthy, and he gave his own meng'an post and all his property to his younger brother Aiboli.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were deeply affectionate. The family was wealthy, and he gave his own meng'an post and all his property to his younger brother Aiboli.

sentences.zh: 愛拔里不肯受，逃避歲餘，阿里終與之。

translations.literal: Aiboli would not accept them and fled for more than a year; in the end Ali gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Aiboli refused to accept them and fled for more than a year, but in the end Ali prevailed upon him to take them.

sentences.zh: 突合速

translations.literal: Tuhesu
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu

sentences.zh: 突合速，宗室子，拿罕塞人。

translations.literal: Tuhesu was a son of the imperial clan, a man of Nahan Sai.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu was a member of the imperial clan, from Nahan Sai.

sentences.zh: 初隸萬戶石家奴麾下，嘗領偏師破雲中諸山寇盜。

translations.literal: At first he served under the wanhu Shijianu and once led a detached force to break the mountain bandits and robbers of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under the wanhu Shijianu and once led a detached force against the mountain bandits of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 宗望攻平州，遣突合速討應州賊，平之，撫安其民而還。

translations.literal: When Zongwang attacked Pingzhou he dispatched Tuhesu to campaign against the Yingzhou rebels, pacified them, soothed and settled the people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang attacked Pingzhou, he sent Tuhesu against the Yingzhou rebels, pacified them, reassured the people, and returned.

sentences.zh: 及伐宋，在宗翰軍，以八謀克破石嶺關屯兵數萬，殺戮幾盡。

translations.literal: When they campaigned against Song he was in Zonghan's army; with eight mouke units he broke the tens of thousands of garrison troops at Shiling Pass and slaughtered nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Song he served in Zonghan's army; with eight mouke units he broke the tens of thousands of garrison troops at Shiling Pass and slaughtered nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 師至太原，祁縣降而復叛，突合速攻下之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Taiyuan, Qi county had surrendered but rebelled again; Tuhesu attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Taiyuan, Qi County had surrendered but rebelled again; Tuhesu attacked and retook it.

sentences.zh: 進取文水縣，後從諸帥列屯汾州之境。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Wenshui county, then followed the various commanders in encamping along the borders of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Wenshui County, then joined the various commanders in encamping along the Fenzhou frontier.

sentences.zh: 宋河東軍帥郝仲連、張思正，陝西軍帥張關索及其統制馬忠，合兵數萬來援，皆敗之。

translations.literal: The Song Hedong army commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Sizheng, the Shaanxi army commander Zhang Guansuo and his commissioner Ma Zhong combined forces numbering in the tens of thousands to come to the relief; he defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Sizheng of the Hedong army, Zhang Guansuo of the Shaanxi army, and Zhang's commissioner Ma Zhong united tens of thousands of relief troops; Tuhesu defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 宗翰南伐至潞還，太原猶未下，即留完顏銀朮可總督諸軍，經略其地。

translations.literal: Zonghan on the southern campaign reached Lu and returned; Taiyuan had still not fallen, so he left Wanyan Yinzhuke to command all armies and administer the region.
translations.idiomatic: Zonghan marched south as far as Lu and returned while Taiyuan still held out; he left Wanyan Yinzhuke in overall command to secure the region.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋援兵大至，突合速從馬五、沃魯破宋兵四千于文水。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song relief troops arrived in great numbers; Tuhesu with Ma Wu and Wolu defeated four thousand Song troops at Wenshui.
translations.idiomatic: Song relief forces then arrived in strength; Tuhesu, with Ma Wu and Wolu, routed four thousand Song troops at Wenshui.

sentences.zh: 聞宋將黃迪等以兵三十萬柵於縣之西山，復與耿守忠合兵九千擊之，殺八萬餘人，獲馬及資糧甚眾。

translations.literal: Hearing that Song generals Huang Di and others with three hundred thousand men had fortified on the western hills of the county, he again joined Geng Shouzhong to combine nine thousand troops and attack them, killing more than eighty thousand men and capturing horses and supplies in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Song generals Huang Di and others had fortified three hundred thousand men on the county's western hills, he joined Geng Shouzhong with nine thousand troops, killed more than eighty thousand, and captured horses and supplies in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 宋制置使姚古率兵至隆州穀，突合速與拔離速以步騎萬餘禦之。

translations.literal: Song commissioner Yao Gu led troops to Longzhou Valley; Tuhesu and Balisu with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: Song commissioner Yao Gu marched to Longzhou Valley; Tuhesu and Balisu met him with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 种師中兵十萬據榆次，銀朮可乃召突合速，使中分其兵而還，與活女等合兵八千擊敗之，斬師中于殺熊嶺。

translations.literal: Zhong Shizhong with one hundred thousand troops held Yuci; Yinzhuke then summoned Tuhesu, had him divide his forces in half and return, and with Huonu and others combined eight thousand troops to defeat them, beheading Shizhong at Shaxiong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Shizhong held Yuci with one hundred thousand men; Yinzhuke recalled Tuhesu, had him split his force and return, then with Huonu and others united eight thousand troops, routed the Song army, and beheaded Shizhong at Shaxiong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 宋將張灝以兵十萬營于文水近郊，復與拔離速擊破之。

translations.literal: Song general Zhang Hao with one hundred thousand troops encamped in the suburbs of Wenshui; he again joined Balisu to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Song general Zhang Hao encamped one hundred thousand men near Wenshui; Tuhesu again joined Balisu and broke them.

sentences.zh: 潞州復叛，宋兵號十七萬，骨赧、突合速、拔離速皆被圍。

translations.literal: Luzhou rebelled again; Song troops were said to number one hundred seventy thousand; Gunan, Tuhesu, and Balisu were all surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou rebelled again, the Song force was said to number one hundred seventy thousand; Gunan, Tuhesu, and Balisu were all encircled.

sentences.zh: 突合速麾軍士，下馬力戰，遂潰圍而出。

translations.literal: Tuhesu directed his soldiers, dismounted and fought with all their strength, and thus broke through the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu ordered his men to dismount and fight with all their strength, and broke out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 及再舉伐宋，宗翰命婁室率軍先趨汴。

translations.literal: When they again raised troops to campaign against Song, Zonghan ordered Lou Shi to lead the army first toward Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin again marched against Song, Zonghan ordered Lou Shi to lead the vanguard toward Bian.

sentences.zh: 婁室至澤州，突合速、沃魯以五百騎爲前驅，往招河陽。

translations.literal: Lou Shi reached Zezhou; Tuhesu and Wolu with five hundred horsemen served as vanguard to go summon Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Shi reached Zezhou; Tuhesu and Wolu rode five hundred horses ahead to summon Heyang to surrender.

sentences.zh: 先據黃河津，宋兵萬余背水陣，進擊敗之，皆擠于水，遂降河陽。

translations.literal: They first seized the Yellow River ford; more than ten thousand Song troops formed a battle line with their backs to the water; advancing they defeated them, all being crowded into the water, and thus Heyang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: They first seized the Yellow River crossing; more than ten thousand Song troops formed a line with their backs to the water. The Jin pressed the attack, drove them into the river, and Heyang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 汴京平，諸將西趣陝津，略定河東郡縣。

translations.literal: When Bianjing was pacified, the generals moved west toward the Shaanxi ford and roughly secured the commanderies and counties of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: After Bianjing fell, the generals turned west toward the Shaanxi crossing and secured the Hedong commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 突合速取憲州，遇其援軍，擊敗之，生擒其將。

translations.literal: Tuhesu took Xianzhou, encountered its relief army, defeated it, and captured its general alive.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu took Xianzhou, routed its relief force, and captured the enemy general alive.

sentences.zh: 孛堇濃瑰朮魯等攻保德，未下，突合速進兵助擊，梯沖並進，遂克其城。

translations.literal: The beijing Nonggui Zhulu and others attacked Baode but had not taken it; Tuhesu advanced to assist the attack; siege ladders and rams advanced together and thus they captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: The beijing Nonggui Zhulu and others besieged Baode without success; Tuhesu marched to assist, siege ladders and battering rams advanced together, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 孛堇烏谷攻石州，屢敗，亡其三將，軍士歿者數百人。

translations.literal: The beijing Wugu attacked Shizhou and was repeatedly defeated, losing three of his generals; several hundred soldiers perished.
translations.idiomatic: The beijing Wugu attacked Shizhou and suffered repeated defeats, losing three generals and several hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 突合速謂烏穀曰：「敵皆步兵，吾不可以騎戰。」

translations.literal: Tuhesu said to Wugu: "The enemy are all infantry; we cannot fight them on horseback."
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu said to Wugu, "The enemy are all foot soldiers—we cannot fight them mounted."

sentences.zh: 烏穀曰：「聞賊挾妖術，畫馬以系其足，疾甚奔馬，步戰豈可及之。」

translations.literal: Wugu said: "I hear the bandits employ sorcery, drawing horses and binding them to their feet; they run as fast as galloping horses—how could infantry combat reach them?"
translations.idiomatic: Wugu replied, "I hear the rebels use sorcery—they draw horses and bind them to their feet and run faster than chargers. How can foot soldiers ever catch them?"

sentences.zh: 突合速笑曰：「豈有是耶!|㚖」乃令諸軍去馬戰，盡殪之。

translations.literal: Tuhesu laughed and said: "How could there be such a thing!" He then ordered all the armies to dismount and fight, and utterly destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhesu laughed and said, "How could there be such a thing!" He then ordered the armies to dismount and fight, and annihilated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 六年，宗輔駐師鄧州，突合速、馬五、拔離速西取均、房，遂下其城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zongfu stationed troops at Dengzhou; Tuhesu, Ma Wu, and Balisu went west to take Jun and Fang, and thus captured those cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, while Zongfu held Dengzhou, Tuhesu, Ma Wu, and Balisu marched west, took Jun and Fang, and captured both cities.

sentences.zh: 攻唐、蔡、陳州及潁昌府，皆克之。

translations.literal: They attacked Tang, Cai, Chenzhou, and Yingchang Prefecture, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked Tang, Cai, Chenzhou, and Yingchang Prefecture and took them all.

sentences.zh: 天眷初，除彰德軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjuan, he was appointed military commissioner of Zhangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianjuan era, he was made military commissioner of Zhangde Army.

sentences.zh: 三年，爲元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, he became left supervisor of the army of the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became left army supervisor on the marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 皇統八年，改濟南尹。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Huangtong, he was transferred to be governor of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Huangtong he was transferred to governor of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 天德間，封定國公，授世襲千戶。

translations.literal: During Tiande, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingguo and granted a hereditary thousand-household fief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiande era he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingguo and granted a hereditary thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，贈應國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yingguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yingguo.

sentences.zh: 初，突合速以次室受封，次室子因得襲其猛安。

translations.literal: Initially, Tuhesu received his enfeoffment through a secondary wife, and the son of the secondary wife therefore inherited his meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tuhesu had received his enfeoffment through a secondary wife, so the secondary wife's son inherited the meng'an.

sentences.zh: 及分財異居，次室子取奴婢千二百口，正室子得八百口。

translations.literal: When they divided property and lived separately, the secondary wife's son took twelve hundred male and female slaves; the primary wife's son received eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When the household divided its property and lived apart, the secondary wife's son took twelve hundred slaves and the primary wife's son eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 久之，正室子爭襲，連年不決，家貲費且盡，正室子奴婢存者二百口，次室子奴婢存者才五六十口。

translations.literal: After a long time the primary wife's son contested the inheritance; for years it remained unresolved; the family's wealth was nearly exhausted—the primary wife's son had only two hundred slaves remaining, and the secondary wife's son had only fifty or sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In time the primary wife's son contested the inheritance; the dispute dragged on for years and nearly consumed the family fortune. The primary wife's son was left with two hundred slaves, the secondary wife's son with only fifty or sixty.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞突合速諸子貧窘，以問近臣，具以爭襲之故爲對，世宗曰：「次室子豈當受封邪!|㚖」遂以嫡妻長子襲。

translations.literal: Shizong heard that Tuhesu's sons were impoverished and questioned his close ministers; they fully explained the reason as the dispute over inheritance. Shizong said: "How could the secondary wife's son receive the enfeoffment!" and had the eldest son of the primary wife inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong heard that Tuhesu's sons had fallen into poverty and questioned his close ministers, who explained the long dispute over the inheritance. Shizong said, "How could a secondary wife's son hold the enfeoffment!" and had the eldest son of the primary wife succeed.

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲盧渾

translations.literal: Wuyan Puluhun
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Puluhun

sentences.zh: 烏延蒲盧渾，曷懶路烏古敵昏山人。

translations.literal: Wuyan Puluhun was a man of Wugu Dihunshan in the Helan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyan Puluhun was from Wugu Dihunshan in the Helan circuit.

sentences.zh: 父孛古剌，龍虎衛上將軍。

translations.literal: His father Beigula was a senior general of the Dragon and Tiger Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Beigula was a senior general in the Dragon and Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 蒲盧渾膂力絕人，能挽強射二百七十步。

translations.literal: Puluhun's physical strength was unmatched; he could draw a strong bow and shoot two hundred seventy paces.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhun's strength was unmatched—he could draw a heavy bow and shoot two hundred seventy paces.

sentences.zh: 與兄鶻沙虎俱以勇健隸闍母軍，居帳下。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Hushahu both, for their courage and vigor, were attached to Zhamu's army and served in his tent entourage.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Hushahu, noted for courage and vigor, entered Zhamu's service and served in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 攻黃龍府，力戰有功。

translations.literal: In the attack on Huanglong Prefecture he fought hard and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Huanglong Prefecture he fought fiercely and earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 闍母敗於兔耳山，張覺復整兵來，諸將皆不敢戰。

translations.literal: Zhamu was defeated at Rabbit-Ear Mountain; Zhang Jue reorganized his troops and came again; none of the generals dared to fight.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhamu was defeated at Rabbit-Ear Mountain, Zhang Jue regrouped and advanced again, and none of the generals dared give battle.

sentences.zh: 蒲盧渾登山望之，乃紿諸將曰：「敵軍少，急擊可破也。

translations.literal: Puluhun climbed the mountain to look at them, then deceived the generals, saying: "The enemy army is small; a swift attack can break them.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhun climbed the hill to reconnoiter, then misled the other generals, saying, "The enemy are few—a quick strike can break them.

sentences.zh: 若入城，不可復製。」

translations.literal: If they enter the city, they cannot be controlled again."
translations.idiomatic: If they reach the city, we shall not be able to stop them again."

sentences.zh: 遂合戰，破之。

translations.literal: They then joined battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They joined battle and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師、蔡靖以燕京降，蒲盧渾率九十騎先伺察城中居民去就。

translations.literal: When Guo Yaoshi and Cai Jing surrendered Yanjing, Puluhun led ninety horsemen first to reconnoiter whether the city's residents would stay or leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Yaoshi and Cai Jing surrendered Yanjing, Puluhun rode ahead with ninety men to see whether the townspeople would stay or flee.

sentences.zh: 遂將漢兵千，隸元顏蒙適攻真定。

translations.literal: He then commanded one thousand Han troops, attached to Wanyan Mengshi in the attack on Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He then led one thousand Han troops under Wanyan Mengshi in the attack on Zhending.

sentences.zh: 進攻贊皇，取之，獲人畜甲仗萬餘。

translations.literal: Advancing he attacked Zanhuang, took it, and captured more than ten thousand persons, livestock, and sets of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing against Zanhuang, he took the city and captured more than ten thousand people, livestock, and sets of arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 汴城破，日已暮，宋人猶力戰，槍刺中蒲盧渾手，戰益力，遂敗宋軍，賜金五十兩。

translations.literal: When Bian city fell, the day was already late; the Song still fought hard; a spear thrust struck Puluhun's hand, yet he fought all the harder and thus defeated the Song army; he was granted fifty taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian fell, night was falling but the Song still fought hard; a spear pierced Puluhun's hand, yet he fought all the harder, broke the Song force, and was rewarded with fifty taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 睿宗爲右副元帥，已定關、陝，議取劍外諸州，遂拔和尚原。

translations.literal: Ruizong served as deputy commander-in-chief on the right; having already secured the passes and Shaanxi, they deliberated taking the prefectures beyond Jian and thus captured Heshangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruizong was deputy commander-in-chief on the right; after securing the passes and Shaanxi, the Jin debated taking the prefectures beyond Jian and captured Heshangyuan.

sentences.zh: 元帥府承制以蒲盧渾爲河北西路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief's headquarters, acting under delegated authority, appointed Puluhun commander-in-chief of all Hebei West Route forces.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters, acting on delegated authority, made Puluhun overall commander of Hebei West Route forces.

sentences.zh: 及宋主在揚州，蒲盧渾與蒙適將萬騎襲之，宋主已渡江，破其餘兵。

translations.literal: When the Song ruler was at Yangzhou, Puluhun and Mengshi led ten thousand horsemen to raid him; the Song ruler had already crossed the river, and they broke his remaining troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song emperor was at Yangzhou, Puluhun and Mengshi led ten thousand horsemen against him; he had already crossed the Yangzi, and they routed his remaining troops.

sentences.zh: 後與斜卯阿里俱從宗弼自淮西渡江取江寧。

translations.literal: Later he together with Xie Mao Ali followed Zongbi from west of the Huai to cross the river and take Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Zongbi with Xie Mao Ali from west of the Huai, crossed the river, and took Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 宗弼入杭州，宋主走明州，再走溫州，由海道追三百餘里，隳明州而歸，語在《阿里傳》。

translations.literal: Zongbi entered Hangzhou; the Song ruler fled to Mingzhou, then fled again to Wenzhou; they pursued by sea route more than three hundred li, dismantled Mingzhou, and returned—the account is in the biography of Ali.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi entered Hangzhou while the Song emperor fled to Mingzhou and then to Wenzhou; they pursued by sea more than three hundred li, dismantled Mingzhou, and returned—the full account is in Ali's biography.

sentences.zh: 天眷二年，授鎮國上將軍，除安國軍，以疾去官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjuan, he was granted the title General Who Pacifies the State and appointed to Anguo Army, but left office due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjuan he was made General Who Pacifies the State and assigned to Anguo Army, but resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 皇統六年，授世襲謀克，起爲延安尹，賜尚衣一襲，尋致仕。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Huangtong, he was granted a hereditary mouke appointment, was recalled as governor of Yan'an, was granted one set of imperial robes, and soon retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Huangtong he received a hereditary mouke, was recalled as governor of Yan'an, was granted a set of imperial robes, and soon retired.

sentences.zh: 海陵遷中都，起爲歸德尹，就其家授之，賜銀牌、襲衣、玉吐鶻，馳驛之官。

translations.literal: When Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, he was recalled as governor of Guide; the appointment was conferred at his home; he was granted a silver tablet, ceremonial robes, and a jade gyrfalcon, and traveled by post relay to take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing moved the capital to Zhongdu, Puluhun was recalled as governor of Guide; the appointment reached him at home along with a silver tablet, ceremonial robes, and a jade gyrfalcon, and he traveled by post relay to take up office.

sentences.zh: 蒲盧渾留數十日，已違程，復聽致仕。

translations.literal: Puluhun remained several tens of days; already past his deadline, he was again permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Puluhun stayed only a few weeks—already past the deadline for taking office—and was again allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 召赴京師，至薊州，見海陵於獵所。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital; reaching Jizhou, he met Hailing at the hunting grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital, he met Hailing at the hunting grounds in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 明日，從獵，獲一狐。

translations.literal: The next day, following the hunt, he caught a fox.
translations.idiomatic: The next day on the hunt he caught a fox.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「卿年老，尚能馳逐擊獸，健捷如此。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Though you are old, you can still gallop in pursuit and strike down game—so vigorous and agile as this."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "You are old, yet you can still gallop in the chase and bring down game—so vigorous and quick as this."

sentences.zh: 賜以禦服，封豳國公。

translations.literal: He was granted imperial robes and enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted imperial robes and enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 除太子少師，進太子太保，改真定尹，入判大宗正事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, promoted to Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, transferred to governor of Zhending, and entered to preside over the Greater Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, promoted to Grand Tutor, transferred to governor of Zhending, and appointed to preside over the Greater Imperial Clan Affairs.

sentences.zh: 頃之伐宋，以本官行右領軍副都督事。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, campaigning against Song, he served in his original post as deputy commander of the Right Army on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on the campaign against Song, he served in his existing post as deputy commander of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 師次西採石，海陵欲渡江，蒲盧渾曰：「宋軍船高大，我船庳小，恐不可遽渡。」

translations.literal: The army halted at West Caishi; Hailing wished to cross the river; Puluhun said: "Song warships are large and tall; our boats are low and small—I fear we cannot cross in haste."
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at West Caishi, Hailing meant to cross the river; Puluhun said, "Song ships are large and high; ours are low and small—I fear we cannot cross at once."

sentences.zh: 海陵怒曰：「汝昔從梁王追趙構於海島，皆大舟耶!|㚖今乃沮吾兵事！

translations.literal: Hailing angrily said: "When you once followed the Prince of Liang in pursuing Zhao Gou to the island in the sea, were they all large boats! Now you dampen my military affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Hailing angrily replied, "When you followed the Prince of Liang in chasing Zhao Gou to the islands, were they all great ships! Now you would discourage my campaign!

sentences.zh: 設不能遽渡江，不過有少損耳。

translations.literal: Even if we cannot cross the river at once, it would be no more than a small loss.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot cross at once, the loss would be slight.

sentences.zh: 爾年已七十，縱自愛，豈有不死理耶。

translations.literal: You are already seventy years old; even if you cherish yourself, is there any principle by which you would not die?
translations.idiomatic: You are seventy; even if you spare yourself, is there any man who does not die?

sentences.zh: 明日當與奔睹先濟。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow I shall cross first with Bendu."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow I shall cross first with Bendu."

sentences.zh: 既而復止之，乃遣別將先渡江，舟小不可戰，遂失利，兩猛安及兵士二百余人皆陷沒。

translations.literal: He then changed his mind and stopped him; he dispatched another general to cross the river first; the boats were too small to fight; they thus suffered defeat, and two meng'an and more than two hundred soldiers were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed his mind and held Puluhun back, sending another general across first; the boats were too small to fight, the crossing failed, and two meng'an with more than two hundred soldiers were lost.

sentences.zh: 海陵遇害，軍還。

translations.literal: Hailing was assassinated; the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing was killed, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，至中都上謁，除東京留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, he arrived at Zhongdu to pay audience and was appointed military governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he came to Zhongdu to pay homage and was appointed military governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗召問年幾何，對曰：「臣今年七十三矣。」

translations.literal: Shizong summoned him and asked how old he was; he replied: "Your subject is seventy-three this year."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong summoned him and asked his age; he answered, "Your subject is seventy-three this year."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿宿將，久練兵事，年雖老，精神不衰。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are a veteran general, long practiced in military affairs; though your years are advanced, your spirit does not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are an old campaigner, long versed in war; though your years are many, your spirit has not faded."

sentences.zh: 因命到官，每旬月一視事。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered that upon taking office he should attend to affairs once every ten-day month.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered that once in office Puluhun need attend to affairs only once each ten-day month.

sentences.zh: 賜衣一襲，進階開府儀同三司，仍封豳國公。

translations.literal: He was granted one set of robes, promoted in rank to Grand Master with the Honor of Opening an Office with Equal Standing to the Three Excellencies, and still enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He received a set of robes, was promoted to Grand Master of the State with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and remained Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 十八年，孫紮虎遷廣威將軍，襲烏古敵昏山世襲猛安，並親管謀克。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, his grandson Zhahu was transferred to General of Expansive Might, inherited the hereditary meng'an of Wugu Dihunshan, and personally administered the mouke as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his grandson Zhahu was made General of Expansive Might, inherited the hereditary meng'an of Wugu Dihunshan, and personally administered its mouke.

sentences.zh: 赤盞暉

translations.literal: Chi Zhanhui
translations.idiomatic: Chi Zhanhui

sentences.zh: 赤盞暉，字仲明，其先附于遼，居張惶堡，故嘗以張爲氏。

translations.literal: Chi Zhanhui, courtesy name Zhongming; his ancestors submitted to Liao and dwelt at Zhanghuang Fort, and therefore sometimes took Zhang as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Zhanhui, styled Zhongming, came of a line that had submitted to the Liao and lived at Zhanghuang Fort, whence they sometimes took Zhang as a surname.

sentences.zh: 後家來州。

translations.literal: Later the family settled at Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later the family settled at Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 暉體貌雄偉，慷慨有志略。

translations.literal: Hui was imposing in build, magnanimous and resolute in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was imposing in stature, open-handed and resolute.

sentences.zh: 少遊鄉校。

translations.literal: In youth he frequented the district school.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied at the district school.

sentences.zh: 遼季以破賊功，授禮賓副使，領來、隰、遷、潤四州屯兵。

translations.literal: In the late Liao, for merit in breaking bandits, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception and commanded garrison troops of the four prefectures of Lai, Xi, Qian, and Run.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Liao, for suppressing bandits he was made Vice Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception and commanded garrison troops in Lai, Xi, Qian, and Run.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年降，仍命領其眾，從闍母定興中府義、錦等州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he surrendered and was still ordered to command his followers; he followed Zhamu in securing Yizhou, Jinzhou, and other prefectures of Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu he submitted and was still allowed to lead his followers; he followed Zhamu in securing Yizhou, Jinzhou, and other prefectures of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 及破張覺，皆與有功，以粟萬五千石助軍，授洺州刺史。

translations.literal: In breaking Zhang Jue he had merit in it all; he supplied fifteen thousand shi of grain to aid the army and was appointed prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in the merit of breaking Zhang Jue, supplied fifteen thousand shi of grain to the army, and was appointed prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宗望初伐宋，孟陽之戰，敵之中軍徑薄宗望營，暉與諸將擊敗之，追殺至城下。

translations.literal: When Zongwang first campaigned against Song, at the battle of Mengyang the enemy's center army pressed straight toward Zongwang's camp; Hui with the generals defeated them and pursued in slaughter to the foot of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang first marched against Song, at Mengyang the enemy center drove straight at Zongwang's camp; Hui and the other generals routed them and pursued to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 訖師還，數立戰功。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended and the army returned, he repeatedly achieved battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army returned, he had won repeated battle honors.

sentences.zh: 明年，再舉伐宋，攻下保州、真定，暉皆與焉。

translations.literal: The next year, when troops were again raised against Song, they attacked and took Baozhou and Zhending; Hui took part in it all.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on the second campaign against Song, they took Baozhou and Zhending, and Hui fought throughout.

sentences.zh: 進圍汴，宋人夜出兵二萬焚我攻具，暉以二謀克兵擊走之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Bian, the Song by night sent out twenty thousand troops to burn our siege engines; Hui with two mouke units attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to besiege Bian, he drove off twenty thousand Song troops who came out by night to burn the siege engines, using two mouke units.

sentences.zh: 凡城中出兵拒戰，暉之所當，無不勝捷。

translations.literal: Whenever troops came out from the city to resist in battle, wherever Hui was assigned, there was none that did not end in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the city sent troops out to fight, wherever Hui was posted the Jin prevailed.

sentences.zh: 既克宋還，從攻河間。

translations.literal: Having conquered Song and returned, he followed in the attack on Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Song he joined the attack on Hejian.

sentences.zh: 敵將李成以雄、莫之兵來援，暉與所部迎擊，馬傷而墮，暉輒奮起步鬥，竟敗成兵。

translations.literal: Enemy general Li Cheng with troops from Xiong and Mo came to the relief; Hui with his detachment went to meet and attack; his horse was wounded and he fell; Hui immediately roused himself to rise and fought on foot, in the end defeating Cheng's troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy general Li Cheng marched from Xiong and Mo to relieve the city, Hui met him with his detachment; his horse was wounded and he fell, but he sprang up and fought on foot until Cheng's force was broken.

sentences.zh: 是日，凡七戰皆勝，敵人多逼死濠隍間，暉兩臂亦數中流矢。

translations.literal: That day, in seven battles all were victories; many of the enemy were forced to death in the moats and ramparts; Hui's both arms also were struck by several arrows in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That day he fought seven engagements and won them all; many enemies were driven to their deaths in the moats, and Hui took several arrows in both arms.

sentences.zh: 賊將劉先生以兵二萬夜襲營，暉力戰達旦，賊始敗走，皆溺死于水。

translations.literal: Bandit general Mr. Liu with twenty thousand troops raided the camp by night; Hui fought hard until dawn; the bandits at last fled in defeat, all drowning in the water.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Liu with twenty thousand men raided the camp by night; Hui fought until dawn and put them to rout, drowning many in the water.

sentences.zh: 暉復傅城力戰，如是連月，諸軍四面合攻，遂克之。

translations.literal: Hui again pressed close to the wall and fought hard; thus for consecutive months the armies on four sides joined in the attack and at last captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui pressed the walls and fought on for months until the armies converged from four sides and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 加桂州管內觀察使，因留撫河間。

translations.literal: He was additionally made intendant within the circuit of Guizhou and remained to administer Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made circuit intendant of Guizhou and remained to pacify Hejian.

sentences.zh: 時居民皆爲軍士所掠，老幼存者亡幾。

translations.literal: At the time the residents had all been plundered by the soldiers; scarcely any old or young remained alive.
translations.idiomatic: By then the people had been plundered by the soldiers until scarcely any old or young survived.

sentences.zh: 暉下令軍中聽贖還之。

translations.literal: Hui ordered throughout the army that redemption be permitted to return them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui ordered the army to allow the people to be ransomed and returned.

sentences.zh: 未幾，皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: Before long, all were settled and tranquil as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the district was settled and at peace again.

sentences.zh: 從睿宗經略山東，既攻下青州，復從闍母攻濰州。

translations.literal: He followed Ruizong in administering Shandong; having attacked and taken Qingzhou, he again followed Zhamu in attacking Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Ruizong in securing Shandong; after Qingzhou fell he again followed Zhamu against Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 暉督其裨校先登，而城中積芻茭乘風縱火發機石，暉率將士沖冒而下，力戰敗之。

translations.literal: Hui directed his officers to ascend first; the city had piled fodder and reeds and sent up fire with the wind and launched catapult stones; Hui led his officers and soldiers to charge down under it and fought hard to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui ordered his officers to scale the walls first; the defenders piled fodder and reeds, set fires on the wind, and hurled catapult stones; Hui led his men through the flames and fighting defeated them.

sentences.zh: 軍還，復以三十騎破敵于範橋。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he again with thirty horsemen defeated the enemy at Fan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he again broke the enemy at Fan Bridge with thirty horsemen.

sentences.zh: 帥府承制加靜江軍節度使。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief's headquarters, acting under delegated authority, additionally appointed him military commissioner of Jingjiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: The marshal's headquarters, acting on delegated authority, additionally made him military commissioner of Jingjiang Army.

sentences.zh: 進攻，城中砲出，幾中暉，拂其甲裳裂之。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack; catapults from within the city were launched and nearly struck Hui, brushing his armor and garments and tearing them.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack; defenders fired catapults from the city that nearly hit Hui, grazing his armor and tearing his garments.

sentences.zh: 暉益奮攻，卒破其城。

translations.literal: Hui fought the attack all the more fiercely and at last broke their city.
translations.idiomatic: Hui redoubled the assault and finally took the city.

sentences.zh: 又從攻泗州，克之。

translations.literal: He again followed in the attack on Sizhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in the attack on Sizhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 還屯汶陽，破賊眾於梁山濼，獲舟千餘。

translations.literal: Returning he garrisoned Wenyang; he broke bandit forces at Liangshan Marsh and seized more than a thousand boats.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he encamped at Wenyang, defeated rebel forces at Liangshan Marsh, and captured more than a thousand boats.

sentences.zh: 移軍攻濟州，既敗敵兵，因傅城諭以禍福，乃舉城降。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to attack Jizhou; having already defeated the enemy troops, he then pressed close to the wall and expounded blessings and calamities, whereupon the whole city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Jizhou; after routing the enemy he paraded before the walls and urged surrender with warnings of ruin, and the city capitulated.

sentences.zh: 暉約束軍士，無秋毫犯，自是曹、單等州皆聞風而下。

translations.literal: Hui restrained the soldiers so that not the slightest offense was committed; from this Caozhou, Shanzhou, and the like all submitted at the mere report of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: Hui kept his troops under strict discipline and allowed no plunder; thereafter Caozhou, Shanzhou, and neighboring prefectures submitted without a fight.

sentences.zh: 從攻壽春、歸德，及渡淮爲先鋒，遇重敵於秀州、蘇州，皆擊敗之，遂至余杭。

translations.literal: He followed in the attacks on Shouchun and Guide; when they crossed the Huai he served as vanguard; encountering strong enemies at Xiu Prefecture and Suzhou he defeated them all and thus reached Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Shouchun and Guide, served as vanguard in the Huai crossing, defeated stiff resistance at Xiu and Suzhou, and advanced as far as Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 通糧餉，治橋道，暉之力爲多。

translations.literal: In opening grain transport, repairing bridges and roads, Hui's exertions were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: He did much of the work of keeping supplies moving and bridges and roads in repair.

sentences.zh: 乃還，載《資治通鑒》版以歸。

translations.literal: He then returned, loading the printing blocks of the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government to carry back.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he brought back the printing blocks of the Zizhi Tongjian.

sentences.zh: 大軍過江寧，徙其官民北渡，時暑多疾疫，老弱轉死道路，其知府陳邦光者訴于宗弼，怒將殺之，暉曰：「此義士也。」

translations.literal: The main army passed through Jiangning and relocated its officials and people to cross north; at the time the summer heat brought much pestilence and the old and weak died one after another on the roads; the prefect Chen Bangguang lodged a complaint with Zongbi, who in anger was about to kill him; Hui said: "This man is a man of righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: When the main army passed through Jiangning and forced officials and civilians north, summer heat and plague left the old and weak dying along the roads. Prefect Chen Bangguang appealed to Zongbi, who angrily ordered his execution. Hui said, "This is a man of honor."

sentences.zh: 力營救之，竟得免。

translations.literal: He exerted himself to rescue him and in the end he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded forcefully on Chen's behalf and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 富平之戰，暉在右翼，遇濘而敗，睿宗念其前功，杖而釋之。

translations.literal: At the battle of Fuping, Hui was on the right wing; encountering mud he was defeated; Ruizong thinking on his prior merit cane-flogged him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuping Hui commanded the right wing and was defeated in the mud; Ruizong, mindful of his earlier service, had him flogged and released.

sentences.zh: 師至熙河，暉別降諸寨將鈐轄及吐蕃酋長等，並民戶萬五千餘。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xihe, Hui on a separate mission induced the surrender of fortress commanders, qianxia officers, and Tibetan chieftains and the like, together more than fifteen thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Xihe, Hui separately induced various fortress commanders, military inspectors, and Tibetan chiefs to submit, along with more than fifteen thousand households.

sentences.zh: 蘭州叛，與訛魯補等攻下之，獲河州安撫使白常、熙河路副都總管劉維輔以獻。

translations.literal: Lanzhou rebelled; together with Elubu and others he attacked and took it, capturing Hezhou Pacification Commissioner Bai Chang and Xihe Circuit Vice Commandant-in-Chief Liu Weifu to present.
translations.idiomatic: When Lanzhou rebelled, he joined Elubu and others in retaking it and sent up as captives Hezhou pacification commissioner Bai Chang and Xihe deputy commander Liu Weifu.

sentences.zh: 還攻慶陽，兩敗重敵，殺其將戴巢。

translations.literal: Returning he attacked Qingyang; twice he defeated strong enemies and killed their general Dai Chao.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he attacked Qingyang, twice routed heavy opposition, and killed the Song general Dai Chao.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷歸德軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to military commissioner of Guide Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was made military commissioner of Guide Army.

sentences.zh: 宋州舊無學，暉爲營建學舍，勸督生徒，肄業者復其身，人勸趨之。

translations.literal: Song Prefecture formerly had no school; Hui for it built school quarters, urged and supervised students; those pursuing study were exempted from corvée labor, and people were encouraged to hasten to it.
translations.idiomatic: Song Prefecture had had no school; Hui built one, urged students to study, and exempted scholars from corvée; enrollment grew quickly.

sentences.zh: 屬縣民家奴王夔者，嘗業進士，暉以錢五十萬贖之，使卒其業，夔後至顯官。

translations.literal: In a subordinate county there was a household slave Wang Kui who had once studied for the jinshi degree; Hui with five hundred thousand cash redeemed him and had him complete his studies; Kui later reached prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: A county slave named Wang Kui had once prepared for the jinshi examinations; Hui paid five hundred thousand cash to free him and see him through his studies, and Wang later rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 密州吏龐乙卒於官，其孤貧，不克葬，暉爲營治葬事，且資給其家。

translations.literal: Pang Yi, a clerk of Mizhou, died in office; his orphans were poor and could not afford burial; Hui for them arranged the funeral and also provided subsidies to the family.
translations.idiomatic: When Mizhou clerk Pang Yi died in office, his orphaned family was too poor to bury him; Hui arranged the funeral and supported the household.

sentences.zh: 十三年，復從大軍渡淮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he again followed the main army in crossing the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he again crossed the Huai with the main army.

sentences.zh: 還鎮，丁母憂，尋以舊職起復。

translations.literal: Returning to his command, he entered mourning for his mother and was soon recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to his post he mourned his mother and was soon recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 既廢齊，爲安化軍節度使。

translations.literal: After Qi was abolished he was made military commissioner of Anhua Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi was abolished he was made military commissioner of Anhua Army.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，復河南，宋人乘間陷海州，帥府以登、萊、沂、密四州委暉經畫，敵無敢窺其境者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan Henan was recovered; the Song seized an opening and took Haizhou; the headquarters entrusted Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi—the four prefectures—to Hui to plan and manage them, and no enemy dared peer into his territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3, when Henan was recovered, the Song seized Haizhou; headquarters entrusted Deng, Lai, Yi, and Mi to Hui, and no enemy dared threaten his territory.

sentences.zh: 爲定海軍節度使，尋改濟南尹，累遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made military commissioner of Dinghai Army, soon transferred to governor of Jinan, and repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military commissioner of Dinghai Army, soon became governor of Jinan, and rose to grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 俄以罪罷。

translations.literal: Shortly he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 久之，起爲昌武軍節度使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised up as military commissioner of Changwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored as military commissioner of Changwu Army.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，遷南京留守，尋改河南路統軍使，授世襲猛安，拜尚書右丞，封河內郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was transferred to military governor of the Southern Capital, soon changed to commander-in-chief of Henan Route, granted a hereditary meng'an, appointed Right Vice Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Prince of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he became military governor of the Southern Capital, then commander-in-chief of Henan Route; he received a hereditary meng'an, was made right vice chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Prince of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜平章政事，封戴王。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Grand Councillor and enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand councillor and enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 正隆初，出爲興平軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenglong he went out as military commissioner of Xingping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenglong he was sent out as military commissioner of Xingping Army.

sentences.zh: 正隆降王爵，爲樞密副使，封景國公。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was reduced; he was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was reduced; he became vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was created Duke of Jing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復爲左丞，封濟國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Left Vice Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made left vice chancellor and created Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 尋除大興尹，封榮國公。

translations.literal: Shortly he was removed to metropolitan prefect of Daxing and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made metropolitan prefect of Daxing and enfeoffed as Duke of Rong.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 大定間諡曰武康。

translations.literal: During the Dading era he was given the posthumous title Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading reign he was given the posthumous title Wukang.

sentences.zh: 子師直，登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Shizhi passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhi passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 大㚖，本名撻不野，其先遼陽人，世仕遼有顯者。

translations.literal: Da Gao, original name Tabuye; his ancestors were men of Liaoyang; for generations they served Liao and had prominent men.
translations.idiomatic: Da Gao, formerly Tabuye, came of Liaoyang stock; his forebears had served the Liao for generations and risen to distinction.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐遼，遼人徵兵遼陽，時㚖年二十餘，在選中。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Liao, the Liao conscripted troops at Liaoyang; at the time Gao was a little over twenty and was among those selected.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked the Liao, the Liao conscripted at Liaoyang; Gao was in his twenties and was drafted.

sentences.zh: 遼兵敗，㚖脫身走甯江。

translations.literal: The Liao army was defeated; Gao escaped and fled to Ningjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao army collapsed, Gao fled to Ningjiang.

sentences.zh: 甯江破，㚖越城而逃，爲軍士所獲，太祖問其家世，因收養之。

translations.literal: When Ningjiang fell, Gao crossed the wall and fled; he was seized by soldiers; Taizu asked about his family background and therefore took him in and raised him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ningjiang fell he scaled the walls to escape but was captured; Taizu questioned him about his lineage and took him into his household.

sentences.zh: 收國二年，爲東京奚民謀克。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shouguo he was made mouke of the Xi people of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Shouguo 2 he was appointed mouke over the Xi people of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，初破高永昌，東京旁郡邑未盡服屬，使㚖伺察反側。
