translations.literal: At that time, having just broken Gao Yongchang, the neighboring prefectures and districts around the Eastern Capital had not all submitted; Gao was sent to watch for unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from defeating Gao Yongchang, the Jin still held only part of the Eastern Capital region; Gao was sent to watch for unrest in the surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 有聞必達，太祖以爲忠實，授猛安，兼同知東京留守事。

translations.literal: Whatever he heard he always reported; Taizu regarded him as loyal and true and appointed him meng'an, concurrently vice commissioner of the Eastern Capital garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He reported everything he learned; Taizu judged him trustworthy and made him meng'an, also deputy commissioner of the Eastern Capital garrison.

sentences.zh: 取中、西兩京，隸闍母軍。

translations.literal: In taking the Central and Western capitals he was attached to Zhamu's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the capture of the Central and Western capitals he served under Zhamu.

sentences.zh: 遼軍二十萬來戰，吳王使㚖以本部守營，㚖堅請出戰，不許。

translations.literal: Two hundred thousand Liao troops came to give battle; the Prince of Wu had Gao with his own unit guard the camp; Gao firmly requested to go out and fight and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When two hundred thousand Liao troops gave battle, the Prince of Wu ordered Gao's unit to guard the camp; Gao begged to fight and was refused.

sentences.zh: 或謂㚖曰：「戰，危事，獨苦請，何也？」

translations.literal: Someone said to Gao: "Battle is a perilous affair—why alone do you plead so bitterly?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Gao, "Fighting is dangerous—why do you alone keep insisting?"

sentences.zh: 㚖曰：「丈夫不得一決勝負，尚何爲。

translations.literal: Gao said: "If a man cannot once decide victory and defeat, what is he worth?
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied, "What is a man worth if he never settles the issue in battle?

sentences.zh: 苟臨戰不捷，雖死猶生也。」

translations.literal: If when facing battle one is not victorious, though one dies one is still alive."
translations.idiomatic: Even defeat in battle is better than never having fought."

sentences.zh: 吳王聞而壯之，乃遣出戰。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wu heard and was impressed; he then sent him out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Wu was stirred by this and sent him into battle.

sentences.zh: 既合戰，闍母軍少卻，遼兵後躡之，㚖麾本部兵橫擊，殺數百人，由是顯名軍中。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, Zhamu's army slightly recoiled and Liao troops pursued from behind; Gao commanded his own unit in a flanking attack and killed several hundred; from this he gained fame in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Zhamu's line fell back and the Liao pressed the pursuit; Gao swung his unit in a flank attack and killed hundreds, winning renown in the army.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，宗望伐宋，信德府居燕、汴之中，可駐軍以濟緩急，欲遂攻之，恐不能亟下，議未決。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui, Zongwang campaigned against Song; Xinde Prefecture lay between Yan and Bian and troops could be stationed there to relieve emergencies; they wished to attack it at once but feared it could not quickly be taken; deliberation was unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 3 Zongwang invaded Song; Xinde Prefecture stood between Yan and Bian and could anchor the army in a crisis, but a direct assault might not succeed quickly and opinion was divided.

sentences.zh: 㚖獨率本部兵，選善射者射其城樓，別以輕銳潛升于樓角之間，遂克其城。

translations.literal: Gao alone led his own unit; selecting skilled archers he had them shoot at the tower on the wall; separately with picked light troops he stealthily ascended between the corner turrets and thus captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gao alone led his unit: sharpshooters pinned the wall towers while picked troops scaled a corner and took the city.

sentences.zh: 明年，軍至浚州，宋人已燒河橋，宗望下令，「軍中有能先濟者功爲上」。

translations.literal: The next year the army reached Xunzhou; the Song had already burned the river bridge; Zongwang issued an order: "Whoever in the army can cross first—merit ranks highest."
translations.idiomatic: The next year at Xunzhou the Song had burned the river bridge; Zongwang proclaimed, "Whoever in the army crosses first will win the highest distinction."

sentences.zh: 㚖捕得十餘舟，使勇悍者徑渡，擊其守者而奪其戍柵，由是大軍俱濟。

translations.literal: Gao captured more than ten boats, had fierce men cross directly, struck their defenders and seized their guard palisade; thus the whole army crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao seized a dozen boats, sent bold men across to rout the defenders and capture the river fort, and the whole army followed.

sentences.zh: 八月，再伐宋，授萬戶，賜金牌。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, campaigning against Song again, he was made wanhu and granted a gold tablet.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the second Song campaign, he was made wanhu and awarded a gold tablet.

sentences.zh: 既破汴京，㚖爲河間路都統。

translations.literal: After Bianjing was taken, Gao was made overall commander of Hejian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Bianjing, Gao became overall commander of Hejian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 已克河間，闍母怒其不早降，因縱軍大掠，㚖諫止之，已掠者官爲贖還。

translations.literal: Having already taken Hejian, Zhamu was angry that it had not surrendered sooner and therefore let the army plunder on a great scale; Gao remonstrated and stopped it; for what had already been plundered the government redeemed and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: After Hejian fell, Zhamu angry at its delay in surrender unleashed a general sack; Gao stopped it and the state ransomed what had already been taken.

sentences.zh: 除河間尹，從攻襲慶府。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Hejian and followed in the attack on Xiqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Hejian and joined the attack on Xiqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先一日，㚖命軍士預備畚鍤及薪，既傅城，諸將方經營攻具，未鳴鼓，㚖軍有素備，遂先登。

translations.literal: One day beforehand Gao ordered soldiers to prepare baskets, shovels, and firewood; once they pressed the wall the generals were still arranging siege engines and had not yet sounded the drum; Gao's army having long been prepared thus ascended first.
translations.idiomatic: A day earlier Gao had his men ready baskets, shovels, and kindling; when the assault began other generals were still preparing siege gear and had not yet sounded the drum, but Gao's troops were ready and scaled the walls first.

sentences.zh: 軍帥以㚖未鳴鼓輒戰，不如軍令，請罪㚖，朝廷釋弗問，仍例賞之。

translations.literal: The army commander, because Gao had fought before the drum without having sounded it, held that this was contrary to military law and requested punishment for Gao; the court released him without inquiry and still rewarded him according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The commander charged Gao with fighting before the drum—a breach of orders—but the court pardoned him and rewarded him as usual.

sentences.zh: 宗弼伐江南，濟淮，宋將時康民率兵十七萬來拒，㚖率本部從擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Zongbi campaigned against Jiangnan and crossed the Huai; Song general Shi Kangmin led one hundred seventy thousand troops to resist; Gao led his own unit in following the attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi crossed the Huai in the Jiangnan campaign, Song general Shi Kangmin met him with one hundred seventy thousand men; Gao joined the attack with his unit and routed them.

sentences.zh: 復以騎二千與當海擊敗淮南賊十萬，殺萬余人，王善來降。

translations.literal: Again with two thousand horsemen together with Danghai he defeated one hundred thousand Huainan bandits, killed more than ten thousand, and Wang Shan came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With two thousand cavalry and Danghai he defeated one hundred thousand Huainan rebels, killed more than ten thousand, and Wang Shan submitted.

sentences.zh: 將渡江，㚖軍先渡，舟行去岸尚遠，宋列兵江口，㚖視其水可涉，則麾兵舍舟趨岸疾擊之，宋兵走，大軍相繼而濟。

translations.literal: About to cross the river, Gao's army crossed first; the boats were still far from shore when the Song drew up troops at the river mouth; Gao seeing the water could be waded commanded the troops to abandon the boats and rush to shore in a swift attack; the Song troops fled and the main army crossed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: As the army prepared to cross the Yangzi, Gao's men led the way; still far from shore they found Song troops massed at the mouth; Gao saw the water was fordable, ordered his men to abandon the boats and charge through the shallows, put the Song to flight, and opened the way for the main force.

sentences.zh: 俄遇杜充兵六萬于江寧之西，㚖與鶻盧補擊走之。

translations.literal: Soon they encountered Du Chong's sixty thousand troops west of Jiangning; Gao together with Hulubu struck and put them to flight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon west of Jiangning they met Du Chong's sixty thousand men; Gao and Hulubu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 師還，㚖留爲揚州都統，經略淮、海、高郵之間。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Gao remained as overall commander of Yangzhou, administering the region between the Huai, the sea, and Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign Gao stayed behind as overall commander of Yangzhou, controlling the Huai coast and Gaoyou region.

sentences.zh: 再爲河間尹，兼總河北東路兵馬。

translations.literal: Again he was made prefect of Hejian, concurrently in overall charge of the military forces of Hebei East Route.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as prefect of Hejian and concurrently commanded Hebei East Route forces.

sentences.zh: 十一年，入見，太宗賜坐，慰勞甚久，特遷太子太保，賜衣一襲、馬二匹及鞍轡鎧甲，改元帥右都監。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he entered court audience; Taizong granted him a seat and consoled and commended him at length; he was specially promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted one suit of clothing, two horses and saddles, bridles, and armor, and made Vice Overseer of the Right of the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was received in audience; Taizong seated him and spoke at length in praise; he was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given clothing, two horses with tack and armor, and made vice overseer of the right under the Marshalate.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，㚖守汴京。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was abolished, Gao guarded Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: When the puppet Qi state was abolished, Gao was left to guard Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 熙宗念㚖久勞，降禦書寵異之。

translations.literal: Xizong thinking on Gao's long labors sent down an imperial letter singling him out for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong, mindful of Gao's long service, sent a personal letter of special favor.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，罷漢、渤海千戶謀克，以㚖舊臣，獨命依舊世襲千戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan the thousand-household mouke posts of Han and Bohai were abolished; because Gao was an old minister he alone was ordered to continue the hereditary thousand-household post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3 the Han and Bohai thousand-household mouke posts were abolished, but Gao as an elder servant was alone allowed to keep his hereditary thousand-household rank.

sentences.zh: 是歲，拜元帥右監軍。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed Right Army Overseer of the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made right army overseer of the Marshalate.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再伐宋，宋人稱臣乞和，遂班師，㚖獨留汴，行元帥府事。

translations.literal: Zongbi again campaigned against Song; the Song people declared themselves subjects and begged for peace; the army then withdrew; Gao alone remained at Bian and conducted the affairs of the marshal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi invaded Song again the Song sued for peace and the army withdrew; Gao alone stayed at Bian to administer the marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangtong he was additionally made Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 3 he was made Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor.

sentences.zh: 八年，進左監軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to Left Army Overseer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to left army overseer.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，改右副元帥，兼行台左丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was changed to Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Right, concurrently Left Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he became vice commander-in-chief of the right and concurrently left vice director of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷平章行台省事，進行台右丞相，右副元帥如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a Grand Councillor of Branch Secretariat affairs, advanced to Right Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat; Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Right remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand councillor of Branch Secretariat affairs and right chancellor of the Branch Secretariat while retaining his post as vice commander-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 海陵疑左副元帥撒離喝，以爲行台左丞相，使㚖伺察之，詔軍事不令撒離喝與聞。

translations.literal: Hailing suspected Left Vice Commander-in-Chief Salihua; appointing him Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, he had Gao watch and investigate him; an edict ordered that in military affairs Salihua was not to be informed.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing distrusted left vice commander Salihua; making him left chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, he set Gao to spy on him and barred Salihua from military deliberations.

sentences.zh: 撒離喝不知海陵意旨，每與㚖爭軍事不能得，遂與㚖有隙。

translations.literal: Salihua did not know Hailing's intent; each time he disputed military affairs with Gao he could not prevail, and thus he and Gao had a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Unaware of Hailing's purpose, Salihua quarreled with Gao over military affairs and lost ground, and the two came to enmity.

sentences.zh: 海陵竟殺撒離喝，召㚖入朝，拜尚書右丞相，封神麓郡王。

translations.literal: Hailing in the end killed Salihua, summoned Gao to court, and appointed him Right Chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, enfeoffing him as Prince of Shenlu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing eventually executed Salihua, recalled Gao to court, made him right chancellor of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Shenlu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年，請老，爲東京留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he requested retirement and was made military governor of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked to retire and was made military governor of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，拜太傅，領三省事，累封漢國王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan he was appointed Grand Tutor, directed the Three Departments, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 he was made grand tutor, directed the Three Departments, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有疾，海陵幸其第問之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he fell ill; Hailing visited his residence to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he fell ill; Hailing visited his home to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: That year he died at sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 海陵親臨哭之，詔有司廢務三日，禁樂三日。

translations.literal: Hailing came in person to mourn him; an edict ordered the offices to suspend business for three days and forbid music for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing mourned him in person and ordered the bureaucracy to suspend business for three days and forbid music for three days.

sentences.zh: 其三日當賜三國使館燕，以不賜教坊樂，命左宣徽使敬嗣暉宣諭之。

translations.literal: On that third day a banquet was due to be granted to the embassies of the three states; because court music was not provided, Left Palace Intendant Jing Sihui was ordered to announce the reason.
translations.idiomatic: On that third day a banquet was due for the three states' embassies; because court music was withheld, Left Palace Intendant Jing Sihui was ordered to explain.

sentences.zh: 贈太師、晉國王，諡傑忠，遣使護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Prince of Jin; his posthumous title was Jiezhong; envoys escorted the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand preceptor and Prince of Jin with the posthumous title Jiezhong; envoys escorted his coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 正隆奪王爵，贈太傅、梁國公。

translations.literal: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was stripped; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenglong his princely rank was revoked; he was posthumously made grand tutor and Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 子磐。

translations.literal: His son was Pan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Pan.

sentences.zh: 磐，本名蒲速越，以大臣子累官登州刺史，襲猛安。

translations.literal: Pan, original name Pusuyue; as the son of a great minister he rose by accumulated offices to prefect of Dengzhou and inherited a meng'an post.
translations.idiomatic: Pan, formerly Pusuyue, was the son of a senior minister; he rose through the ranks to prefect of Dengzhou and inherited a meng'an post.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，除嵩州刺史，從僕散忠義伐宋有功。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he was made prefect of Songzhou; following Pusan Zhongyi in campaigning against Song he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 he was appointed prefect of Songzhou and served with distinction under Pusan Zhongyi against the Song.

sentences.zh: 五年，召爲符寶郎，遷拱衛直都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned as Master of Seals and Talismans and transferred to Chief Commander of the Arch Guardian Direct Unit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled as master of seals and talismans and promoted to chief commander of the Arch Guardian Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，磐以伐宋功，進官一階，磐心少之，頗形於言。

translations.literal: At first, for his merit in campaigning against Song, Pan was advanced one rank in office; Pan's heart thought it too little and this showed considerably in his speech.
translations.idiomatic: At first Pan received only one rank for his service against the Song; he considered it slight and said so openly.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，下吏按問，杖一百五十，改左衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and handed him to officials for investigation; he was caned one hundred fifty strokes and made Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, officials investigated; Pan was flogged one hundred fifty strokes and demoted to Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 詔求良弓，磐多自取，及護衛入直者，輒以己意更代。

translations.literal: An edict sought fine bows; Pan took many for himself; moreover when palace guards entered duty he arbitrarily replaced them according to his own wishes.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought good bows Pan helped himself to many; he also swapped out guards on palace duty at his own whim.

sentences.zh: 護衛婁室告其事，詔點檢司詰問。

translations.literal: Palace guard Loushi reported the matter; an edict ordered the Inspection Office to question him.
translations.idiomatic: Guard Loushi reported him; the Inspection Office was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 磐有妹在宮中爲寶林，磐屬內侍僧兒員思忠使言于寶林曰：「我無罪，問事者迫我，使自誣服。」

translations.literal: Pan had a younger sister in the palace serving as Baolin; Pan had the inner attendant Seng'er Yuansizhong speak to Baolin, saying: "I am guiltless; those questioning the matter force me to confess falsely against myself."
translations.idiomatic: Pan's sister served in the palace as Baolin; Pan had the eunuch Seng'er Yuansizhong tell her, "I am innocent—the investigators are forcing me to incriminate myself."

sentences.zh: 寶林訴於上，上怒，杖僧兒一百，磐責隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: Baolin complained to the emperor; the emperor was angry, caned Seng'er one hundred strokes, and demoted Pan to defender of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Baolin appealed to the emperor, who had Seng'er flogged one hundred strokes and banished Pan to defender of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「汝在近密，執迷自用，朕以卿父之功，不忍廢棄，姑令補外，其思勉之。」

translations.literal: The emperor admonished him, saying: "You are close to inner secrets yet persist in obstinacy and self-will; for your father's merit I cannot bear to cast you off; for the moment I order you to fill an outside post—reflect on this and exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warned him: "You hold a post close to the throne yet insist on your own way; for your father's sake I will not discard you utterly—take an outside assignment and consider your conduct."

sentences.zh: 改亳州防禦使，遷武甯軍節度使，坐事除名。

translations.literal: He was changed to defender of Bozhou, transferred to military commissioner of Wuning Army, and on account of an offense was dismissed from office and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was made defender of Bozhou, then military commissioner of Wuning Army, and was eventually stripped of rank for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 起爲韓州刺史。

translations.literal: He was raised up as prefect of Hanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as prefect of Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 改祁州刺史，復坐事，削四官，解職。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Qizhou; again on account of an offense four ranks were stripped and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qizhou, again ran afoul of the law, lost four ranks, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，尚書省奏「大磐以年當敘」，上曰：「剛暴之人，屢冒刑章，不可復用。

translations.literal: After a long time the Department of State Affairs memorialized that "Great Pan by years is due for advancement in rank"; the emperor said: "A violent and fierce man who repeatedly violates the penal code cannot be employed again.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the Department of State Affairs recommended Da Pan for routine advancement; the emperor replied, "Violent men who repeatedly break the law cannot be restored.

sentences.zh: 太傅大㚖，別無嫡嗣，其世襲猛安謀克，不可易也。」

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Da Gao has no other legitimate heir; his hereditary meng'an and mouke may not be altered."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Da Gao has no other legitimate heir; his hereditary meng'an and mouke must not pass to anyone else."

sentences.zh: 阿離補，宗室子，系出景祖。

translations.literal: Alibu was a clansman, descended from Jingzu.
translations.idiomatic: Alibu was a clansman descended from Jingzu.

sentences.zh: 屢從征伐，滅遼舉宋皆有功。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns; in destroying Liao and raising Song he had merit in all.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns and distinguished himself in the conquest of Liao and Song.

sentences.zh: 天會九年，睿宗經略陝西，阿離補爲左翼都統，與右翼都統宗弼撫定鞏、洮、河、西寧、蘭、廓等州軍，來賓、定遠、和政、甘峪、甯洮、安隴等城寨，及鎮、堡、蕃、漢營部四十餘處，漢官軍民蕃部酋長甚眾，於是涇原、熙河兩路皆平。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianhui, Ruizong conducted operations in Shaanxi; Alibu was left-wing commander-in-chief; together with right-wing commander-in-chief Zongbi he pacified the prefectures and armies of Gong, Tao, He, Xining, Lan, Kuo, and the like, the forts of Laibin, Dingyuan, Hezheng, Ganyu, Ningtao, Anlong, and the like, and more than forty towns, forts, and Tang and Han encampments; Han officials, soldiers, civilians, and tribal chieftains were very numerous; thus both Jingyuan and Xihe circuits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 9, when Ruizong conducted operations in Shaanxi, Alibu served as left-wing commander-in-chief; with right-wing commander Zongbi he pacified Gong, Tao, He, Xining, Lan, Kuo, and other prefectures and armies, forts including Laibin, Dingyuan, Hezheng, Ganyu, Ningtao, and Anlong, and more than forty towns, forts, and Tang and Han encampments, bringing many Han officials, soldiers, civilians, and tribal chiefs to submission; both Jingyuan and Xihe circuits were thereby pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔以兄猛安沙離質親管謀克之餘戶，以阿離補爲世襲謀克。

translations.literal: An edict granted the remaining households of the mouke personally administered by his elder brother, meng'an Shalizhi, and made Alibu hereditary mouke.
translations.idiomatic: An edict assigned the remaining households of the mouke administered by his elder brother, meng'an Shalizhi, and made Alibu hereditary mouke.

sentences.zh: 天會十二年，爲元帥右都監。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianhui he was made vice overseer of the right under the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 12 he was made vice overseer of the right under the Marshalate.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷左監軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to left army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to left army overseer.

sentences.zh: 天眷三年，從宗弼復河南，遷左副元帥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjuan he followed Zongbi in recovering Henan and was transferred to left vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjuan 3 he followed Zongbi in recovering Henan and was made left vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 皇統三年，封譚國公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangtong he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 3 he was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 六年，爲行台左丞相，元帥如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made left chancellor of the Branch Secretariat, his post as commander-in-chief remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made left chancellor of the Branch Secretariat while retaining his commander-in-chief post.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 大定間，大褒功臣，圖像衍慶宮。

translations.literal: During the Dading era, meritorious ministers were greatly honored and their portraits placed in Yanqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading reign meritorious ministers were lavishly honored with portraits enshrined in Yanqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 歡都死康宗時，不及與馳騖遼、宋之郊，然而異姓之臣莫先焉。

translations.literal: Huandu died in the time of Kangzong and did not reach the age of racing through the borders of Liao and Song; yet among ministers of other surnames none came before him.
translations.idiomatic: Huandu died under Kangzong before the campaigns against Liao and Song, yet among non-Jurchen ministers none ranked before him.

sentences.zh: 故定衍慶亞次功臣：代國公歡都，金源郡王石土門，徐國公渾黜，鄭國公謾都訶，濮國公石古乃，濟國公蒲查，韓國公斜卯阿里，元帥左監軍拔離速，魯國公蒲察石家奴，銀青光祿大夫蒙適，隨國公活女，特進突合速，齊國公婆盧火，開府儀同三司烏延蒲盧渾，儀同三司阿魯補，鎮國上將軍烏林答泰欲，太師領三省事勖，太傅大㚖，大興尹赤盞暉，金吾衛上將軍耶律馬五，驃騎衛上將軍韓常並阿離補鹹著勳焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the second-tier meritorious ministers at Yanqing were fixed as follows: Huandu, Duke of Dai; Shimen, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Hunchu, Duke of Xu; Manduhe, Duke of Zheng; Shigunai, Duke of Pu; Pucha, Duke of Ji; Xie Mao Ali, Duke of Han; Balisu, Left Army Overseer of the Marshalate; Pucha Shijianu, Duke of Lu; Meng Shi, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon; Huonü, Duke of Sui; Tuhesu, Special Advancement; Poluhuo, Duke of Qi; Wuyan Puluhun, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Alubu, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Ulin Da Taiyu, General-in-Chief Who Guards the State; Xu, Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments; Da Gao, Grand Tutor; Chi Zhanhui, Metropolitan Prefect of Daxing; Yelü Mawu, General-in-Chief of the Jinwu Guard; Han Chang, General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard; and Alibu were all enshrined for their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: The second rank at Yanqing Palace was therefore set as: Huandu, Duke of Dai; Shimen, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Hunchu, Duke of Xu; Manduhe, Duke of Zheng; Shigunai, Duke of Pu; Pucha, Duke of Ji; Xie Mao Ali, Duke of Han; Balisu, left army overseer of the Marshalate; Pucha Shijianu, Duke of Lu; Meng Shi, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon; Huonü, Duke of Sui; Tuhesu, Special Advancement; Poluhuo, Duke of Qi; Wuyan Puluhun, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Alubu, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Ulin Da Taiyu, General-in-Chief Who Guards the State; Xu, Grand Preceptor directing the Three Departments; Da Gao, Grand Tutor; Chi Zhanhui, metropolitan prefect of Daxing; Yelü Mawu, General-in-Chief of the Jinwu Guard; Han Chang, General-in-Chief of the Flying Cavalry Guard; and Alibu—all were enshrined for their merit.

sentences.zh: 子言、方，言別有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Yan and Fang—Yan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yan and Fang; Yan has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 子 方

translations.literal: Son: Fang
translations.idiomatic: Fang

sentences.zh: 方以宗室子累官京兆少尹，遷陝西路統軍都監。

translations.literal: Fang, as a member of the imperial clan by accumulated offices, rose to Vice Prefect of the Capital District of Jingzhao and was transferred to Overall Commander of the Shaanxi Circuit Army.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, a clansman who rose through accumulated appointments, became vice prefect of the Jingzhao capital district and was transferred to overall commander of the Shaanxi circuit army.

sentences.zh: 方專事財賄，不恤軍旅，詔戒之曰：「卿宗室舊人，乃縱肆敗法，惟利是營，朕甚惡之。

translations.literal: Fang devoted himself to bribes and did not care for the army; an edict admonished him, saying: "You are an old clansman, yet you indulge yourself and break the law, seeking profit alone—I greatly detest this.
translations.idiomatic: Fang trafficked in bribes and neglected military affairs; the emperor warned him, "You are an old clansman, yet you break the law for profit—I find this repugnant.

sentences.zh: 自今至於後日，萬一爲之，必罰無赦。」

translations.literal: From now until days to come, if you do such a thing even once, punishment will be without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: If you do this again, from this day forward, you will be punished without mercy."

sentences.zh: 大定三年，遷元帥右都監，轉元帥左監軍，改順天軍節度使，上曰：「卿本無功，曆顯仕，不能接僚友，往往交惡，在京兆貪鄙彰聞，至無謂也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading he was transferred to Vice Overseer of the Right of the Marshalate, then to Left Army Overseer of the Marshalate, and changed to military commissioner of Shuntian Army; the emperor said: "You originally had no merit yet passed through prominent offices; you cannot get on with colleagues and often quarrel with them; in Jingzhao your greed and baseness were notorious—this is utterly pointless.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3 he was made vice overseer of the right under the Marshalate, then left army overseer, then military commissioner of Shuntian Army; the emperor said, "You had no merit yet held high office, quarreled constantly with colleagues, and in Jingzhao your greed was notorious—this is absurd.

sentences.zh: 朕念卿已過中年，必能悛改，慎勿復爾。」

translations.literal: I think on you as already past midlife and surely able to reform—take care not to do so again."
translations.idiomatic: You are past middle age; I expect you to mend your ways—do not repeat this."

sentences.zh: 除西南路招討使，朝廷以兵部郎中高通爲招討都監，以佐之。

translations.literal: He was made Pacification Commissioner of the Southwest Route; the court appointed Gaotong of the Bureau of Military Affairs as Pacification Vice Commissioner to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed pacification commissioner of the Southwest Route; the court named Military Affairs Bureau director Gaotong pacification vice commissioner to assist him.

sentences.zh: 詔通曰：「卿到天德，毋以其官長曲從之也。

translations.literal: An edict to Gaotong said: "When you reach Tiande, do not defer to him because he is your superior officer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Gaotong, "When you reach Tiande, do not yield to Fang simply because he outranks you.

sentences.zh: 簡閱沿邊士卒，毋用孱弱之人，毋以僕隸代役。

translations.literal: Review the border soldiers; do not employ weaklings; do not substitute servants for corvée duty.
translations.idiomatic: Inspect the border troops: do not keep weak men, and do not let servants stand in for military service.

sentences.zh: 女直舊風，凡酒食會聚，以騎射爲樂。

translations.literal: The old Jurchen custom was that at wine feasts and gatherings, riding and archery were the entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: By Jurchen custom, feasts were for riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 今則弈棋雙陸，宜悉禁止，令習騎射。

translations.literal: Now they play chess and backgammon; these should all be forbidden and riding and archery made the practice.
translations.idiomatic: Chess and backgammon have taken over; forbid them and restore riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 從其居處之便，亦不可召集擾之。」

translations.literal: Follow what is convenient to their dwellings; do not summon and harass them either."
translations.idiomatic: Let men train where they live; do not summon them needlessly and disturb them."

sentences.zh: 久之，方坐強買部人馬二匹，削一階，解職，降耀州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time Fang on account of forcibly buying two horses from a subordinate was stripped of one rank, removed from office, and demoted to prefect of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Fang was demoted one rank, dismissed, and made prefect of Yaozhou for forcibly buying two horses from a subordinate.

sentences.zh: 通亦坐贓除名。

translations.literal: Gaotong also on account of corruption was dismissed and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gaotong was also stripped of rank for corruption.

sentences.zh: 方後遷橫海軍節度使，人爲同簽大宗正事，簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Fang was later transferred to military commissioner of Henghai Army, also served as co-signer of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and signed documents for the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fang later became military commissioner of Henghai Army, also served as co-signer of the Court of the Imperial Clan, and as signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，阿魯補當授謀克，未封而薨，烏帶受之。

translations.literal: At first Alubu was to receive the mouke, but before he was enfeoffed he died and Wu Dai received it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Alubu was to receive the mouke, but he died before enfeoffment and Wu Dai received it.

sentences.zh: 烏帶死，兀答補襲之。

translations.literal: When Wu Dai died, Wudabu inherited it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Dai died, Wudabu inherited it.

sentences.zh: 兀答補死，烏也阿補當襲。

translations.literal: When Wudabu died, Wuye'abu was to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wudabu died, Wuye'abu was due to inherit.

sentences.zh: 是時，已降海陵爲庶人，世宗以烏帶在熙宗逆黨中，其子孫不合受封，停封者久之，而阿離補功亦不可廢絕，特詔方襲之雲。

translations.literal: At that time Hailing had already been reduced to commoner status; Shizong, because Wu Dai was among Xi Zong's traitorous faction, held that his descendants were unfit to receive enfeoffment, and the grant was suspended for a long time; yet Alibu's merit could not be extinguished, and a special edict had Fang inherit it, as stated.
translations.idiomatic: By then Hailing had been demoted to commoner status; Shizong held that Wu Dai's descendants, as members of Xi Zong's conspiracy, were unfit to inherit, and the grant was long suspended—yet Alibu's merit could not be set aside, so a special edict had Fang inherit it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：斜卯阿里、突合速、烏延蒲盧渾、赤盞暉、大㚖、阿離補等六人，皆收國以來所謂熊羆之士、不二心之臣也，其功有可錄者焉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Xie Mao Ali, Tuhesu, Wuyan Puluhun, Chi Zhanhui, Da Gao, and Alibu—these six men—all since Shouguo have been called warriors like bears and tigers, ministers of undivided loyalty; their achievements are worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Xie Mao Ali, Tuhesu, Wuyan Puluhun, Chi Zhanhui, Da Gao, and Alibu—since Shouguo bear-and-tiger warriors and loyal-hearted ministers all—performed deeds worth recording.
